---
name: ddx
description: Operates the DDx toolkit for document-driven development. Covers beads (work items), the queue, executions, agents, harnesses, personas, reviews, spec-id. Use when the user says "do work", "drain the queue", "run the next bead", "execute a bead", "review this", "check against spec", "what's on the queue", "what's ready", "create a bead", "file this as work", "run an agent", "dispatch", "use a persona", "how am I doing", "ddx doctor", or mentions any ddx CLI command.
---

# DDx

DDx (Document-Driven Development eXperience) is a CLI platform for
document-driven development. It ships a bead tracker (portable work
items with acceptance criteria), an agent service (harness dispatch
with profile-first routing), a persona system (bindable AI
personalities), a library registry (plugins with prompts, templates,
personas), and git-aware synchronization. This skill makes any
skills-compatible coding agent (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini
CLI, etc.) understand and operate the DDx surface correctly.

## How this skill works

The skill body you're reading is an **overview** plus an **intent
router**. The real domain guidance lives in `reference/*.md` files.

**Directive: before responding to any DDx-related request, read the
matching reference file from the router table below. The router is
not optional — your answer must be grounded in the reference file's
guidance, not this overview alone.**

## Vocabulary

Single source of truth for DDx terms. Every reference file uses these
exact definitions.

- **Bead** — a portable work item (task, bug, epic, chore) with
  metadata, dependencies, and acceptance criteria. `ddx bead create`.
- **Queue** — the set of open beads. The *ready queue* is the subset
  with all dependencies closed. `ddx bead ready`, `ddx bead blocked`.
- **Ready** — a bead whose dependencies are all closed and which is
  eligible to be picked up next. `ddx bead ready`.
- **Blocked** — a bead with at least one unclosed dependency.
  `ddx bead blocked`.
- **Claim** — mark a bead as in-progress by an agent (concurrent-write
  protection). `ddx bead update <id> --claim`.
- **Close** — mark a bead as done, with evidence (session, commit
  SHA). `ddx bead close <id>`. Beads only close on execution outcomes
  `success` or `already_satisfied`.
- **Work** — drain the bead queue. `ddx work` (alias for
  `ddx agent execute-loop`); see `reference/work.md`.
- **Execute-bead** — the primitive: run one agent on one bead in an
  isolated worktree. `ddx agent execute-bead <id>`. The loop wraps
  this.
- **Execute-loop** — the queue-drain orchestrator; picks ready beads
  one at a time, calls execute-bead, closes on success, unclaims on
  failure. `ddx agent execute-loop` (or `ddx work`).
- **Execution** — a generic DDx execution run (FEAT-010); broader
  than execute-bead. Includes execution definitions, execution
  records, and execution evidence under `.ddx/executions/<id>/`.
- **Agent** — an AI coding agent (Claude, Codex, Gemini, etc.)
  invoked via a harness. Not a subagent (harness-specific — see
  below).
- **Harness** — the abstraction DDx uses to dispatch an agent
  (subprocess for claude/codex/gemini; embedded for the built-in
  `agent` harness). `ddx agent list`, `ddx agent capabilities`.
- **Persona** — a Markdown file (YAML frontmatter + body) that
  defines an AI personality. DDx injects the body as a system-prompt
  addendum to `ddx agent run`. `ddx persona list/show/bind`.
- **Role** — an abstract function (e.g., `code-reviewer`,
  `test-engineer`) a workflow can reference. Projects bind roles to
  personas.
- **Binding** — a project-specific `role: persona` map in
  `.ddx/config.yaml` under `persona_bindings`.
- **Profile** — intent-based routing policy for `ddx agent run`:
  `cheap` (low-cost), `fast` (low-latency), `smart` (balanced
  default). `--profile cheap|fast|smart`.
- **Plugin** — a self-contained extension installed to
  `.ddx/plugins/<name>/`. The default `ddx` plugin (personas,
  prompts, patterns, templates) is auto-installed by `ddx init`.
  `ddx install <name>`.
- **Skill** — an agentskills.io-standard directory (SKILL.md +
  optional `reference/`, `evals/`, `scripts/`). This `ddx` skill is
  the one DDx ships. Plugins can ship additional skills.
- **Subagent** — a harness-local concept for running a prompt in an
  isolated context (Claude Code's `.claude/agents/` + `context:
  fork`; Codex's `agents/`; others differ). DDx's `ddx agent run`
  (especially with `--quorum`) is the portable primitive; how a
  harness wraps that in a subagent is harness business. This skill
  does not take a position on subagent orchestration.
- **Update** — refresh plugin/toolkit content to a newer version.
  `ddx update [<plugin>]`.
- **Upgrade** — replace the DDx binary with a newer release.
  `ddx upgrade`.
- **Review** — two distinct concepts. **Bead review**
  (`ddx bead review <id>`) grades a completed bead against its
  acceptance criteria. **Quorum review** (`ddx agent run
  --quorum=<policy> --harnesses=<list>`) dispatches a review prompt
  across multiple harnesses and aggregates. See `reference/review.md`.
- **Governing artifact** — the document that authorizes a bead's
  work: a FEAT-\*, SD-\*, TD-\*, or ADR-\* under `docs/`. Referenced
  via `spec-id`.
- **Spec-id** — the `spec-id: <ID>` custom field on a bead pointing
  at its governing artifact.

## Intent router

Before responding, read the matching file.

| User says / asks about | Read this file |
|---|---|
| write/plan work, "create a bead", "file this as work", bead metadata, acceptance criteria, dependencies | `reference/beads.md` |
| "do work", "drain the queue", "run the next bead", "execute a bead", "run work", verify-and-close | `reference/work.md` |
| "review this", "check against spec", bead review, quorum review, code review, adversarial check | `reference/review.md` |
| "run an agent", "dispatch", harnesses, profiles, models, effort, "use a persona", role bindings | `reference/agents.md` |
| "what's on the queue", "what's ready", "how am I doing", health check, "ddx doctor", sync status | `reference/status.md` |

If the intent spans multiple files (e.g., "create a bead and then
run it"), read beads.md first, then work.md. If no match, ask the
user which concept they mean rather than guessing.

## Top-level policy reminders

These apply across all DDx operations. Do not restate them in every
reference file; do not violate them.

- **Never edit `.ddx/beads.jsonl` directly.** All tracker changes go
  through `ddx bead create/update/close/dep`. Direct edits corrupt
  bead history and cannot be audited.
- **Tracker changes are commit-worthy.** After `ddx bead create`,
  `update`, `dep add/remove`, or `close`, commit the resulting
  `.ddx/beads.jsonl` change — either as a tracker-only commit or
  folded into the same commit as related implementation changes.
- **Preserve execute-bead commit history.** Branches containing
  `ddx agent execute-bead` commits carry an audit trail. **Never
  squash, rebase, filter, or amend** these commits. Use only
  `git merge --ff-only` or `git merge --no-ff` when merging.
  `gh pr merge --squash` and `--rebase` are forbidden on these
  branches.
- **Work in worktrees for parallel agents.** Use `wt switch -c
  <branch>` (worktrunk) or equivalent to give each concurrent agent
  its own isolated checkout. Execute-bead does this automatically;
  manual parallel work should too.
- **Profile-first agent dispatch.** Default to
  `ddx agent run --profile smart` (or `cheap`/`fast` for specific
  intents). Only override with `--harness`/`--model`/`--effort`
  when pinning for a controlled test or known provider bug.

## Links out

- Full CLI reference: `ddx --help`, `ddx <subcommand> --help`.
- Governing feature specs: see `FEAT-*` documents under your
  project's `docs/` tree — especially the CLI, beads, agent-service,
  executions, and skills features.
- Personas README: shipped by the default `ddx` plugin at
  `.ddx/plugins/ddx/personas/README.md`.
- Open standard this skill conforms to:
  [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io).

# Work — Drain the Queue, Execute, Verify, Close

"Doing work" in DDx means draining the ready queue: pick the top
ready bead, dispatch an agent, verify the result, and close the bead
on success (or unclaim it on failure).

## Default surface: `ddx work`

```bash
ddx work
```

`ddx work` is an alias for `ddx agent execute-loop`. It drains the
queue by picking the top ready bead, running it through
`ddx agent execute-bead`, and advancing to the next one. Prefer this
over running individual commands.

Flags worth knowing:

- `--once` — pick one bead and stop (don't loop).
- `--poll-interval <dur>` — continuous worker mode; wait between
  iterations.
- `--harness <name>` — force a specific harness (overrides profile).
- `--profile cheap|fast|smart` — routing intent (default `smart`).
- `--model <ref>` — exact model pin (overrides profile).
- `--local` — run inline in the current process (no subprocess).

## Primitive: `ddx agent execute-bead`

For targeted re-runs, debugging, or running a specific bead:

```bash
ddx agent execute-bead <bead-id>
ddx agent execute-bead <bead-id> --from <rev>      # base commit override
ddx agent execute-bead <bead-id> --no-merge        # preserve result, don't land
```

`execute-bead` runs an agent against one bead in an isolated git
worktree. It's what `ddx work` calls under the hood.

## Pick by default, not by ID

Under normal operation, **don't specify a bead ID**. `ddx work` picks
the top ready bead based on priority + dependency satisfaction. Only
pin a specific ID when debugging (`ddx agent execute-bead <id>`) or
when the queue ordering would pick the wrong bead and you need to
override.

## Verify independently before closing

**Agents hallucinate successful completions.** Do not trust the
agent's self-report. Before closing a bead:

1. Run the acceptance-criteria command yourself (from the bead's
   `accept:` field). If it's `go test ./foo/...`, run that.
2. Check the resulting commit against the in-scope file list from
   the bead description. Out-of-scope files touched? Reject the
   attempt.
3. Read the commit message — does it reference the bead ID?
   (`[ddx-<id>]` or similar in the commit subject is the convention.)

If all three pass: close the bead.

## Close on success, unclaim on failure

DDx execute-bead outcomes form a specific taxonomy. Each outcome
maps to a concrete follow-up action:

| Outcome | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `success` | Tests pass, AC met, commit landed | `ddx bead close <id>` |
| `already_satisfied` | No changes needed (AC was already green) | `ddx bead close <id>` |
| `no_changes` | Agent returned without producing commits | Leave open, **unclaim** |
| `land_conflict` | Merge conflict on landing the result | Leave open, **unclaim** |
| `post_run_check_failed` | Tests or gate failed after landing | Leave open, **unclaim**, investigate |
| `execution_failed` | Agent subprocess errored (timeout, crash, provider error) | Leave open, **unclaim** |
| `structural_validation_failed` | Result failed structural sanity check | Leave open, **unclaim**, investigate |

`ddx work` applies these actions automatically. If you're running
`execute-bead` directly, apply them manually: `ddx bead update <id>
--unclaim` to release a bead after a non-closing outcome, so another
worker can pick it up.

**Never leave a bead half-owned** — every execution either closes or
unclaims.

## Testing expectations for bead implementations

When an agent implements a bead, its output should include tests
that exercise the new code:

- **Unit tests** for logic with in-memory stubs for first-party
  collaborators. Favor stubs over mocks; mocks that assert on call
  sequences test implementation, not behavior.
- **Integration tests** against real collaborators where the cost
  is small (real git in a temp dir, real DB in a temp file, real
  HTTP via a local test server).
- **Real e2e tests** at the outermost boundary. E2e tests that mock
  the database or the network are unit tests lying about their
  scope.
- **Coverage measurement only where the project tracks it.** Don't
  introduce coverage tooling just for one bead; use what the
  project already has. Coverage is a signal, not a target.
- **Performance claims require baselines.** If the bead's AC
  mentions "faster" or "scales", the acceptance test must include:
  (a) a numeric baseline, (b) an explicit boundary (what's
  measured, what's excluded), (c) a reproducible harness.

## Anti-patterns

- **Trusting the agent's "done"**: always re-run the AC command
  yourself before closing.
- **Closing on no_changes**: only `success` and `already_satisfied`
  close a bead. `no_changes` means the agent returned without doing
  anything — unclaim and investigate.
- **Squashing execute-bead commits**: the per-attempt history is
  an audit trail (evidence commits, heartbeats). Use only
  `git merge --ff-only` or `--no-ff`; never squash/rebase/filter.
- **Running `--harness` without a reason**: profile-first routing
  (`--profile smart`) picks a reasonable default. Override only
  when pinning for a bug repro or controlled test.
- **Parallel workers on the same claimed bead**: the tracker
  guards against this via claim semantics, but don't try to defeat
  it — each claim represents an in-flight attempt.

## CLI reference

```bash
ddx work                                    # default queue drain
ddx work --once                             # one bead, then stop
ddx work --poll-interval 30s                # continuous worker
ddx work --harness claude --profile smart   # pin harness, profile

ddx agent execute-bead <id>                 # primitive
ddx agent execute-bead <id> --from <rev>    # override base commit
ddx agent execute-bead <id> --no-merge      # preserve iteration

ddx agent execute-loop                      # same as ddx work
```

Full flag list: `ddx work --help`, `ddx agent execute-bead --help`.

docs/research/qwen3.6-27b-cross-provider-2026-04-27.md:95:**This is the critical local result.** The lucebox slowness is *not* a hardware problem — vanilla llama.cpp on the same GPU does the same job in 5 s. It's a tuning gap on Blackwell consumer (sm_120) per the upstream README, which explicitly says "Blackwell/Ada not yet swept, PRs welcome". For production use today on this hardware, **LM Studio is the right choice** — it's competitive with the cloud baseline (5.2 s vs 4.9 s).
docs/research/qwen3.6-27b-cross-provider-2026-04-27.md:101:The cloud baseline (openrouter Alibaba-hosted qwen3.6-plus) is **~3.3× faster than vidar**, ~7× faster than grendel, ~23× faster than lucebox on this set. Expected — the cloud Qwen-plus runs on optimized inference infra. Not a fair single-machine comparison, but it sets the practical ceiling and the realistic floor for local inference latency.
docs/research/qwen3.6-27b-cross-provider-2026-04-27.md:157:The cloud baseline doesn't pay these costs at the same rate because (a) faster per-token throughput, (b) Qwen-plus's reasoning is more concise on this task class, (c) the agent's tool-execute side runs locally so model + tool overlap better with cloud latency.

Audit note: other Anthropic-specific fields (metadata keys, system placement, etc.) checked during this fix; any additional leaks filed as follow-up beads.","created_at":"2026-04-18T01:59:49.083741699Z","description":"## Summary\n\nThe agent library sends an Anthropic-specific `thinking` field in OpenAI-compatible request bodies to non-Anthropic providers (lmstudio, omlx, openrouter, ollama). Providers that accept and parse the request then silently terminate their SSE stream after the first delta frame when their generation pipeline encounters the unknown field. Downstream consumers see `unexpected end of JSON input`.\n\nThis bug was classified via wire capture using the new AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE=1 flag (this repo's agent-941e7e42, landed in v0.3.12). Evidence was gathered from DocumentDrivenDX/ddx ddx-6a5dfe35.\n\n## Wire evidence (v0.3.12, 2026-04-18)\n\n```\nPOST http://vidar:1235/v1/chat/completions\nContent-Type: application/json\nBody includes:\n  \"stream\":true,\n  \"stream_options\":{\"include_usage\":true},\n  \"thinking\":{\"budget_tokens\":8192,\"type\":\"enabled\"},\n  \"tools\":[... 6 tools ...],\n  \"model\":\"Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit\"\n```\n\nResponse:\n- HTTP 200\n- Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8\n- Body captured: 186 bytes total\n  - Frame 1: `: keep-alive\\n\\n` (SSE keepalive)\n  - Frame 2: valid `data: {...\"delta\":{\"role\":\"assistant\"}}\\n\\n` (assistant role start)\n  - Then: stream terminates. No `data: [DONE]`. No error frame. Just EOF.\n\n`thinking` is Anthropic's extended-thinking API. It is NOT in the OpenAI chat-completions schema. vidar-omlx (OpenAI-compatible, no Anthropic semantics) has no handler for it and its generation pipeline fails silently mid-stream.\n\nReproduced on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit AND Qwen3-Coder-Next-MLX-4bit — model-independent. Reproduced across two projects (ddx repo + agent repo) — project-independent. Reproduced on v0.3.11 and v0.3.12 — both versions exhibit the bug.\n\n## Root cause\n\nThe openai-compat provider's request-serialization path does not gate flavor-specific fields. `thinking` is serialized into the wire body unconditionally when the caller has passed the equivalent Anthropic-style configuration (via preset or CLI flag). Since v0.3.12 now has Provider.DetectedFlavor() (agent-92f0f324), the library has the information it needs to gate this — it just doesn't use it in the serializer.\n\n## Fix direction\n\nIn the openai-compat provider's Chat/ChatStream request builder:\n\n1. Before writing the request body, check `p.DetectedFlavor()`.\n2. If the flavor is NOT one that supports Anthropic thinking semantics (i.e., NOT `anthropic-passthrough` or similar — in practice all current openai-compat flavors: lmstudio, omlx, openrouter, ollama, plus `openai-native`), omit the `thinking` field from the serialized JSON.\n3. Emit a debug log (at Trace level or via AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE when that flag is on) noting that `thinking` was stripped for flavor X. Operators should see this when diagnosing 'why isn't my local model using thinking'.\n\nThe anthropic provider package continues to include the field in its own serializer (no change there).\n\nLong term, consider a broader per-flavor field allowlist/denylist in the openai-compat serializer — `thinking` is probably not the only Anthropic-specific field that leaks. Audit the request builder for other non-portable fields.\n\n## Alternative (less preferred)\n\nReject at config-load: if Config passes `thinking` config AND any provider in the same config has a non-Anthropic DetectedFlavor, emit a startup warning. Does not help when providers are added at runtime and does not handle the case where a single agent run targets multiple providers with different flavors in the same session.\n\nStripping at serialization is cleaner.\n\n## Other non-portable fields likely to have the same issue\n\nThese are candidates for the same per-flavor gate:\n- `metadata` with Anthropic-specific keys\n- `system` as a top-level field vs in messages array (OpenAI uses messages[].role=system; some providers may tolerate both, some may not)\n- `anthropic_version` or similar API-version fields\n- Extended-thinking budget controls beyond `thinking`\n\nAudit as part of the fix; file follow-up beads if other fields exhibit the same symptom.\n\n## Related\n\n- agent-92f0f324 (v0.3.12): DetectedFlavor() — this fix consumes it\n- agent-941e7e42 (v0.3.12): AGENT_DEBUG_WIRE — this bug was classified using it\n- agent-767549c7 (v0.3.12): capability flags — related but orthogonal (capability gating wouldn't have prevented this specific leak)\n- DocumentDrivenDX/ddx ddx-6a5dfe35: consumer bead tracking the symptom; closes when this upstream bead lands + DDx bumps dep.","id":"agent-04639431","issue_type":"bug","labels":["agent","kind:bug","area:provider","area:openai-compat","area:serialization"],"priority":0,"status":"closed","title":"provider: strip Anthropic-specific fields (thinking) from non-Anthropic request bodies using DetectedFlavor() gate","updated_at":"2026-04-18T02:06:00.744147214Z"}

Consumer migration note published.","claimed-at":"2026-04-20T03:59:51Z","claimed-machine":"eitri","claimed-pid":"994875","created_at":"2026-04-20T03:48:09.234052812Z","description":"Surfaced while migrating ddx (consumer) from ddx-agent v0.5.0 → v0.6.0 (see DDx tracker ddx-4535f466; sibling agent bead agent-117a0868).\n\n## Argument\n\nv0.6.0 added `ProviderPreference` (`LocalFirst` / `SubscriptionFirst` / `LocalOnly` / `SubscriptionOnly`) to `RouteRequest` as the consumer-facing placement knob. This sits in an uncanny valley:\n\n- It's **too abstract to be a real choice** — a caller who cares enough about placement to set it usually has more specific intent (\"only local because I'm offline\", \"cloud because this one task is worth $2\", \"openrouter-haiku for this batch because I know the shape\"). The 4-value enum can't express any of that.\n\n- It's **too specific to delegate** — a caller who doesn't want to think about placement shouldn't have to pick one of four values at every call site. The right default depends on tier, cost budget, connectivity, and user policy — none of which `ProviderPreference` sees.\n\n- Every consumer that plumbs it through ends up re-deriving the same tier→preference translation (cheap → LocalFirst, smart → SubscriptionFirst), which is (a) duplicated across consumers, (b) guaranteed to drift, and (c) not tunable without a code change.\n\n## The richer abstraction that already almost exists: profiles\n\nA profile is a named bundle of multi-axis policy. Examples of what profiles can express that `ProviderPreference` can't:\n\n- `cheap`: prefer local; fall back to openrouter-haiku; never opus; stall-kill aggressively; cap reasoning at 2k tokens\n- `offline`: local-only; fail loud if no local provider; no network calls at all\n- `smart-but-cheap`: subscription-first but only models under $5/Mtok input\n- `air-gapped`: local-only + disable telemetry + reject any http provider\n- `code-high`: any provider, coding-tuned models, reasoning=high, prefer large context\n\n`ProviderPreference` reduces all of that to one axis. A profile is a data structure, and data structures compose.\n\nv0.6.0's `models.yaml` already has `surface_policy` per target carrying `effort_default` and `reasoning_default`. Extending that to carry placement order, cost ceilings, and failure policy is an additive change; the shape is already there.\n\n## Proposal\n\n1. **Remove `RouteRequest.ProviderPreference`** from the public service surface (v0.7.0 breaking change; acceptable now because adoption is low and we're already mid-migration).\n2. **Reinstate profiles as the consumer-facing routing knob.** `RouteRequest.Profile` (or let `ModelRef` carry a profile name — today `ModelRef` already accepts tier names like `cheap`/`standard`/`smart`, so this may be a simple semantic consolidation, not a new field).\n3. **Move placement policy into profile/catalog definitions.** Each profile/target declares its own candidate providers, candidate models, placement order, reasoning defaults, cost ceilings, and failure policy. Users retune by editing one file (`models.yaml` or user override).\n4. **Pinpoint control stays as an escape hatch.** Callers that already know the exact provider + model pass `Provider` + `Model` directly and bypass the profile machinery entirely. That's the \"if I'm going to micromanage I'll just set the provider\" path — preserved, not denied.\n5. **No per-call-site policy expression.** Consumers that don't know placement don't have to decide it. The profile does.\n\n## Why this matters for the consumer side\n\nDDx's ddx-4535f466 Track B was originally \"audit every `ResolveRoute` call site and add the right `ProviderPreference`.\" If this proposal lands, that track collapses to zero: callers either use a profile (and the agent decides placement) or pin Provider+Model (and they own placement). No middle layer for DDx to translate.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n1. `RouteRequest.ProviderPreference` removed from the public surface; `ProviderPreference` constants no longer exported.\n2. Profiles (named, multi-axis policy bundles) are the documented public routing knob. CONTRACT-003 updated.\n3. `surface_policy` in `models.yaml` carries placement order + cost ceilings + failure policy, not just reasoning defaults.\n4. A consumer wanting \"local-first cheap\" sets `Profile: \"cheap\"` and the catalog's cheap profile expresses \"prefer local, fall back to openrouter-haiku\". A consumer wanting pinpoint control sets `Provider` + `Model` and bypasses the profile machinery.\n5. Migration note in CHANGELOG for any v0.6.0 consumer that started using `ProviderPreference`.","execute-loop-heartbeat-at":"2026-04-20T03:59:51.212118813Z","id":"agent-285a05d2","issue_type":"task","labels":["area:service","area:routing","area:catalog","kind:design","phase:design"],"owner":"erik","priority":1,"status":"closed","title":"RouteRequest.ProviderPreference is the uncanny valley — reinstate profiles as the public routing knob","updated_at":"2026-04-20T04:03:32.072580045Z"}

The *ready queue* is the subset\\n  with all dependencies closed. `ddx bead ready`, `ddx bead blocked`.\\n- **Ready** — a bead whose dependencies are all closed and which is\\n  eligible to be picked up next. `ddx bead ready`.\\n- **Blocked** — a bead with at least one unclosed dependency.\\n  `ddx bead blocked`.\\n- **Claim** — mark a bead as in-progress by an agent (concurrent-write\\n  protection). `ddx bead update \u003cid\u003e --claim`.\\n- **Close** — mark a bead as done, with evidence (session, commit\\n  SHA). `ddx bead close \u003cid\u003e`. The loop wraps\\n  this.\\n- **Execute-loop** — the queue-drain orchestrator; picks ready beads\\n  one at a time, calls execute-bead, closes on success, unclaims on\\n  failure. `ddx agent execute-loop` (or `ddx work`).\\n- **Execution** — a generic DDx execution run (FEAT-010); broader\\n  than execute-bead. Includes execution definitions, execution\\n  records, and execution evidence under `.ddx/executions/\u003cid\u003e/`.\\n- **Agent** — an AI coding agent (Claude, Codex, Gemini, etc.)\\n  invoked via a harness. Used for high-stakes or adversarial checks. |\\n\\n## Bead review\\n\\n```bash\\nddx bead review \u003cbead-id\u003e\\n```\\n\\nGenerates a review-ready prompt that includes:\\n\\n- Bead title, description, acceptance criteria (verbatim).\\n- Governing artifact content (follows `spec-id`).\\n- The diff since the bead's base commit (execution evidence commits\\n  excluded — see the related bug ddx-39e27896 for exclusion\\n  pathspec).\\n- Review instructions: output contract, verdict taxonomy.\\n\\nThe reviewer (whoever receives the prompt — a human, a harness via\\n`ddx agent run`, or a quorum) produces a structured verdict:\\n\\n```\\n## Bead review: ddx-\u003cid\u003e\\n\\n### Verdict: APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | BLOCK\\n\\n### Per-criterion\\n\\n1. [AC text]\\n   Verdict: APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | BLOCK\\n   Evidence: \u003cfile:line, test output, diff hunk, or explicit \\\"not verifiable\\\"\u003e\\n\\n2. [AC text]\\n   ...\\n\\n### Summary\\n\u003c1-3 sentences of overall context\u003e\\n\\n### Findings\\n\u003cdetailed issues, if any; omit when verdict is APPROVE with no findings\u003e\\n```\\n\\nThe review output can be stored as bead evidence:\\n\\n```bash\\nddx bead evidence add \u003cid\u003e --type review --body \u003cpath-to-review.md\u003e\\n```\\n\\n## Quorum review\\n\\n```bash\\nddx agent run --quorum=majority --harnesses=claude,codex,gemini \\\\\\n  --prompt review-prompt.md\\n```\\n\\n`--quorum=\u003cpolicy\u003e` values:\\n\\n- `majority` — at least ⌈N/2⌉ harnesses must agree on the verdict.\\n- `unanimous` — all harnesses must agree.\\n- `any` — pass if any harness APPROVES (rarely useful; adversarial\\n  checks should require stronger consensus).\\n\\nUse quorum when:\\n\\n- The change is high-stakes (migrations, security surface, API\\n  contracts, auth).\\n- The review surface is controversial and one harness's opinion\\n  isn't enough.\\n- You want adversarial pressure against a single-model blindspot\\n  (different model families have different failure modes).\\n\\nThe aggregated output shows each harness's verdict side-by-side plus\\nthe aggregate decision. Disagreements are surfaced, not hidden.\\n\\n## Required evidence format\\n\\nBoth review kinds share an evidence contract: **no verdict without\\nevidence.**\\n\\n- \\\"APPROVE\\\" with no `Evidence:` lines → reject as malformed.\\n- \\\"REQUEST_CHANGES\\\" without pointing at the change needed → reject.\\n- \\\"BLOCK\\\" without a reason → reject (see the related bug\\n  ddx-39e27896 about `review-malfunction` retries).\\n\\nEvidence takes one of these forms:\\n\\n1. **File:line reference**: `cli/internal/bead/store.go:142`\\n2. **Test output**: `FAIL: TestBeadClose_UnclaimsOnNonSuccess (0.01s)`\\n3. **Diff hunk**: a short quote from the diff showing the offending\\n   or approved change.\\n4. **Explicit \\\"not verifiable\\\"**: the AC is written in a way that\\n   cannot be mechanically checked; flag this as a bead-authoring\\n   issue rather than silently approving.\\n\\n## Anti-patterns\\n\\n- **Hallucinated approval.** \\\"Looks good to me!\\\" with no per-AC\\n  grading. (5) Regression test uses a mock LM Studio that lists 'qwen/foo' but rejects 'foo' on chat/completions; discovery normalizes 'foo' → 'qwen/foo' and the probe succeeds.","closed_at":"2026-04-16T00:00:00Z","closing_commit_sha":"7632714","created_at":"2026-04-15T04:50:46.518311375Z","description":"Discovered 2026-04-15 while routing work to vidar-coder (LM Studio on vidar:1234).\n\n## Two-part bug\n\n### Part 1: bare-name JIT miss (the actual root cause)\n\nInitial probe: `POST /v1/chat/completions {model: 'qwen3-coder-next', ...}` → 400 'No models loaded'.\n\nWe assumed LM Studio had no model loaded. Wrong. The actual model is listed by /v1/models as 'qwen/qwen3-coder-next' (with the 'qwen/' prefix). LM Studio's just-in-time loading IS enabled and DOES auto-load models on demand — but only when the requested model ID matches one in /v1/models exactly. Bare-name 'qwen3-coder-next' didn't match, so JIT couldn't fire, and LM Studio returned the misleading 'No models loaded' error instead of 'unknown model'.\n\nVerified by re-probing with 'qwen/qwen3-coder-next' — JIT fired, model loaded, responded 'OK' in ~60s on cold start.\n\n### Part 2: discovery should be standard practice\n\nThe routing/probe layer should never trust user-supplied bare model names against an LM Studio provider. The standard discovery flow should be:\n\n1. GET /v1/models → enumerate the catalog the server is offering\n2. For each catalog ID, optionally probe POST /v1/chat/completions with a 1-token request and a generous timeout (60s+ on cold start, 3s on warm)\n3. Cache the (provider, model_id) → inference-ready bool with a short TTL\n4. When user code asks for 'model qwen3-coder-next' against this provider, normalize against the discovered catalog: if there's exactly one match by suffix, accept it; if zero or multiple, error with the candidate list\n\nThis converts the 'No models loaded' misleading error into a clear 'requested model qwen3-coder-next not in catalog; closest match: qwen/qwen3-coder-next' (or just transparent normalization).\n\n## Impact on cost-tiered routing\n\nThe cost-tiered routing policy (DDx bead ddx-dc231144 tier-based auto-escalation) needs reliable provider readiness signals. Without discovery + normalization:\n- bare-name configs silently fail and force escalation\n- the 'connected (N models)' status is unreliable as a routing input\n- every misrouted attempt burns latency and forces the next tier\n\n## Fix scope\n\n- Update routing/health probe in cmd/ddx-agent/routing.go (or equivalent) to enumerate /v1/models and probe each listed model with its exact ID\n- Add a model-id normalization layer that maps bare names to catalog IDs by suffix-match (with explicit error on ambiguity)\n- Cache probe results per (provider, model) for a short TTL (30s reasonable)\n- Surface the distinction in 'ddx-agent providers' output: http-connected (from /v1/models) vs inference-ready-models (the subset that actually responds)","events":[{"actor":"ddx","body":"{\"resolved_provider\":\"claude\",\"resolved_model\":\"claude-opus-4-6\",\"fallback_chain\":[]}","created_at":"2026-04-16T12:55:30.616994974Z","kind":"routing","source":"ddx agent execute-bead","summary":"provider=claude model=claude-opus-4-6"}],"id":"agent-40ee5960","issue_type":"bug","labels":["kind:bug","area:routing","area:discovery","provider:lmstudio"],"priority":1,"resolution":"fixed: /v1/models discovery + bare-name normalization in provider/openai","status":"closed","title":"bug: /v1/models is not a liveness probe — providers shows 'connected' when LM Studio has no model loaded","updated_at":"2026-04-16T12:55:30.627873415Z"}
